deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from 34r): m = a+bi is a Gaussian integer with odd norm p = a^2+b^2 ≡ 1 (mod 4). In the intended application m is prime and a, b are coprime. The least residues mod m are the μ with μ/m = x+iy, 0 ≤ x,y < 1. The nonzero ones fall into four classes: f (x<1/2, y<1/2), f' (x>1/2, y<1/2), f'' (x>1/2, y>1/2) and f''' (x<1/2, y>1/2). Each class has (p-1)/4 members. One gets f' = i f + m, f'' = -f + (1+i)m and f''' = -i f + i m. For M prime to m, M^{(p-1)/4} ≡ i^ε (mod m). Gauss calls ε the 'Decident' of M mod m.

(4) Theorem (biquadratic Gauss lemma). Multiply each element of f by M and reduce mod m to its least residue. Let α, β, γ, δ be the numbers of these residues lying in f, f', f'', f''' respectively. Then ε ≡ β + 2γ + 3δ (mod 4).

Proof as on the page, with the implicit steps filled in [mine]:
- Partition f into g, g', g'', g''' according to the class of the residue of gM.
- If g'M ≡ r' ∈ f', then r' = i s + m with s ∈ f, so -i g'M ≡ s ∈ f. Likewise -g''M and i g'''M have residues in f.
- These residues are pairwise distinct and distinct from those of gM. [Mine: e.g. gM ≡ -i g'M would give g' ≡ i g, but the residue of i g lies in f' while g' lies in f.]
- There are (p-1)/4 of them in total, so they are a permutation of f. Hence ∏_{g∈f} g ≡ ∏(gM)·∏(-i g'M)·∏(-g''M)·∏(i g'''M) = (∏ f)·M^α (-iM)^β (-M)^γ (iM)^δ.
- ∏ f is a unit mod m, so M^α (-iM)^β (-M)^γ (iM)^δ ≡ 1.
- That is, M^{(p-1)/4}(-i)^β(-1)^γ i^δ ≡ 1, so M^{(p-1)/4} ≡ i^β(-1)^γ(-i)^δ = i^{β+2γ+3δ}.
- [Mine: i^ε ≡ i^k mod a non-unit odd m forces ε ≡ k (mod 4), since the units 1, i, -1, -i are incongruent mod m.]

(5) Class test. Let ω be the componentwise floor of N/m, a Gaussian integer. The least residue is N - ωm, with N/m - ω = x+iy in [0,1)^2. So the class is read off from whether x, y are below or above 1/2. Then the integer part of 2N/m equals 2ω + [2x] + i[2y]. In the four cases this is 2ω, 2ω+1, 2ω+1+i, 2ω+i. Hence (as 34r's sequel states) the class is determined by the parities of ξ, η in [2N/m] = ξ + ηi. This leads to Dec(M/m) = Σ Θ(2fM/m), a lattice-point count analogous to Eisenstein's form of Gauss's lemma. Note that x = 1/2 or y = 1/2 cannot occur: 2Re(μ m̄) = p is impossible for odd p.
errors: In item 5 the manuscript lists the integer parts of 2N/m as 2ω, 2ω-1, 2ω-1-i, 2ω-i. With ω the floor of N/m (so that N - ωm is the least residue with x,y ≥ 0) they should be 2ω, 2ω+1, 2ω+1+i, 2ω+i. Signs are a slip (or ambiguous strokes). Harmless: the parity criterion drawn on the next page is unaffected.
Distinctness of the residues of gM, -ig'M, -g''M, ig'''M is asserted without proof. It is easy: it follows from the class maps f→f', f'', f''' on 34r.
The final step from M^{(p-1)/4} ≡ i^{β+2γ+3δ} to ε ≡ β+2γ+3δ (mod 4) silently uses that the four units are incongruent mod m. This holds since N(m) > 2 is odd.
Tacit hypotheses: m is prime (or at least the Euler-type congruence holds), gcd(a,b)=1 (excluded on 34r), and M is prime to m.

results.what: For m in Z[i] of odd norm p and M prime to m, with β, γ, δ the numbers of residues M·f falling in the 'quadrants' f', f'', f''': M^{(p-1)/4} ≡ i^{β+2γ+3δ} (mod m)
results.modern_name: Gauss's lemma for biquadratic (quartic) residues in Z[i]
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Nachlass, published in Werke II); in print such quartic lemmas were developed by Eisenstein and later authors

results.what: Class of the least residue of N determined by parities of real and imaginary parts of the integer part of 2N/m, leading to Dec(M/m) = Σ Θ(2fM/m)
results.modern_name: Eisenstein-type lattice-point (floor-function) reformulation of Gauss's lemma, Gaussian-integer version
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Nachlass); the rational analogue from Gauss's third proof of quadratic reciprocity (1808) and Eisenstein

deep.surprise_reason: This is the quartic analogue of Gauss's lemma in Gauss's own 'Decident' terminology. Such Nachlass material on biquadratic residues is printed in Werke II and discussed in the literature (e.g. Lemmermeyer, Reciprocity Laws). It is a nice unpublished-in-his-lifetime detail but already known as Gauss's.

checkable.asserts: The class maps f'=if+m, f''=-f+(1+i)m, f'''=-if+im for m=1+2i.
